value.text:
We are given claims and evidence. We need to check each claim against the cited evidence. We must flag only factual problems: overstatements, wrong numbers/dates/suppliers, causes not stated, products/NDCs not in evidence. Reasonable conclusions from cited facts are supported.

We'll go through each claim.

Claim 1: investigator: "Our package NDC 0409-4279-02 is listed on the FDA shortage list as "Available" updated 10/21/2026." Cited: [shortage-0409-4279-02]. Evidence says exactly that. Supported.

Claim 2: investigator: "Current stock is 394 units covering 13.6 days at 29 units per day, with a backordered order of 325 units expected 2026-10-24." Cited: [stock-2]. Evidence says: "394 units on hand, 29/day over 30 days, 13.6 days of cover; open orders: PO-SAMPLE-002 backordered 325 units from Cardinal Health, expected 2026-10-24". Matches. Supported.

Claim 3: investigator: "An ongoing FDA Class II recall by Hospira, Inc. (recall-D-1815-2015) cites particulate matter (iron oxide) in glass vials." Cited: [recall-D-1815-2015]. Evidence says: "FDA recall D-1815-2015 (Class II, ongoing) by Hospira, Inc.: Presence of Particulate Matter: particulate matter identified as iron oxide, was found embedded in the neck of glass vials." Matches. Supported.

Claim 4: substitution: "Current lidocaine 10 mg/mL from Hospira has 13.6 days of cover." Cited: [stock-2]. Evidence says 13.6 days of cover. Supported.

Claim 5: substitution: "Current lidocaine 10 mg/mL is therapeutically equivalent (TE code AP) per Orange Book." Cited: [ob-ANDA088329-001]. Evidence says: "Orange Book: LIDOCAINE HYDROCHLORIDE 1% (INJECTABLE;INJECTION) by HOSPIRA INC, application ANDA088329, TE code AP (our current product)". Supported.

Claim 6: substitution: "Substitute ANDA203082 is therapeutically equivalent (TE code AP) to current product." Cited: [ob-ANDA203082-001, ob-ANDA088329-001]. Evidence: ob-ANDA203082-001 says TE code AP for EUGIA PHARMA SPECIALITIES LTD ANDA203082. ob-ANDA088329-001 says TE code AP for Hospira. Both have TE code AP, so they are therapeutically equivalent to each other? The claim says "Substitute ANDA203082 is therapeutically equivalent (TE code AP) to current product." Since both have TE code AP, they are considered therapeutically equivalent to the reference listed drug. Usually, if both are AP, they are considered therapeutically equivalent to each other. The claim is a reasonable conclusion. However, the evidence does not explicitly state they are equivalent to each other; but the Orange Book TE code AP means they are therapeutically equivalent to the reference listed drug. The claim is a reasonable conclusion from the cited facts. So supported.

Claim 7: substitution: "Substitute ANDA203082 has at least one package at our concentration listed as Available on the FDA shortage list." Cited: [status-ANDA203082]. Evidence says: "Checked EUGIA PHARMA SPECIALITIES LTD ANDA203082: 5 package(s) at our concentration in a comparable presentation in the FDA product listing ... 55150-163-30 by Eugia US LLC: FDA shortage list "Available"); no ongoing recall on these products. Result: on the FDA shortage list, but at least one package at our concentration is listed as Available." So supported.

Claim 8: substitution: "EUGIA PHARMA SPECIALITIES LTD ANDA203082: Therapeutically equivalent (TE code AP) with at least one package Available on the FDA shortage list and preservative-free while ours is not." Cited: [status-ANDA203082, ob-ANDA203082-001, ob-ANDA088329-001, ndc-55150-163, ndc-80425-0268]. Let's check each part:
- Therapeutically equivalent (TE code AP): ob-ANDA203082-001 says TE code AP. Supported.
- At least one package Available on FDA shortage list: status-ANDA203082 says at least one package (55150-163-30) is Available. Supported.
- Preservative-free while ours is not: status-ANDA203082 says "This product is preservative-free; ours is not." Supported.
- The claim also mentions EUGIA PHARMA SPECIALITIES LTD ANDA203082. That's consistent.
All parts supported.

Thus all claims are supported. No unsupported claims.
